Bond markets brace for AI borrowing

By Ada Example

France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as inflation bites. With large technology companies now issuing billions in bonds to pay for data centres, they are competing with governments for the same investors.

Analysts say the extra supply could push up the cost of borrowing across the euro area, even for countries with strong public finances. Some governments have already shortened the length of the debt they sell.

"It is a question of who gets the money first," one fund manager said. "Governments have always assumed there would be room for them, and that is no longer certain."

The central bank has said it is watching the effect on borrowing costs, but has not signalled any change to its plans. Read the explainer for background.
